Miss Minnie Halsell, who served as primary assistant during the last year, or perhaps the last two years, of the history of the school, was the daughter of President Halsell and had received her training in the College under the administration of her father. Soon after the dissolution of the institution, she married Mr. William Phipps, and they moved to the Indian Territory, where she died about 1894.


MUSIC AND ART TEACHERS

Of the teachers of the fine arts in connection with the Savoy College the two who remained longest were connected with the institution in its early years—Madame Michely and Mrs. Jnd Mathison.

Miss Lou Arterberry of Savoy gives a brief but striking picture of Madame Michely in the following excerpts from letters to the author:

Madame Michely was of pure Spanish stock, born, reared, and educated in Madrid, was highly accomplished in music, she played everything—guitar, violin, harp, and piano—in any key, transposing and playing them all with equal fluency. She had married a Frenchman and lived for a long time in Havana, Cuba, before coming to this country. . . .

She came to Savoy with a colony of educated people to establish a school there, bringing with them this part of their plan. However, they were unable to secure their plan, and the colony met with reverses and the school was never founded. . . . She made her home at Burmida's hotel in Savoy, where she did private teaching and supported herself for a time by running a modest little store. She died a few years later from injuries sustained in the storm in the year of the cyclone.
